question: Where can I get a list of solar PV plants in operation in the United States, with location, capacity (MW), operator and commissioning date?

answer.summary: EIA-860 (final 2025) lists 7,979 operating PV generators at 7,309 plants (152,848 MW AC) in 49 states and DC, with plant coordinates, operator (Utility Name) and commercial operation month and year. EIA-860M (September 2026): 8,335 generators, 7,651 plants, 170,562 MW AC, plus Puerto Rico on separate sheets. USGS USPVDB v4.0 (14 April 2026), downloaded from USGS, maps 6,611 ground-mounted facilities of 1 MW or more linked to EIA plant codes. Under 1 MW there is no plant list: EIA gives estimates by state; LBNL's Tracking the Sun covers about 4.0 million systems by ZIP code, with no operator.
main_caveats: Scope: EIA-860 and EIA-860M cover plants of 1 MW or more combined nameplate; 76 PV plants in the annual file have under 1 MW AC of PV (47 list other generators, 29 none). Small-scale PV has no EIA plant list.
Capacity: EIA nameplate is AC; DC at STC is in the solar sheet (198,471 MW DC against 152,848 MW AC). USPVDB threshold is on DC: 52 of 6,611 records have AC under 1 MW, none have DC under 1 MW.

Date: EIA 'Operating Month/Year' is initial commercial operation per generator; the plant date used here is the earliest. LBNL COD for Topaz (2014-10-31) matches the latest generator. USPVDB p_year is not independent of EIA.
Operator: 'Utility Name' is the company responsible for day-to-day operations, not the owner. 'Entity Name' in EIA-860M differs from it for 190 of 8,307 generators in annual plants.
Location: EIA gives a central point of the property; USPVDB v4.0 gives polygons and a representative point (median gap 0.22 km; 213 matched plants above 5 km; maximum 333 km).

Version: USPVDB v4.0 contains 6,611 facilities; 57 do not match any operating PV plant in the 2025 or September 2026 EIA files, and the EIA files hold 1,064 PV plants of 1 MW or more that v4.0 does not map.
answer.confidence_reason: EIA-860 2025, EIA-860M (September 2026), USPVDB v4.0 and LBNL's utility-scale file were downloaded and checked. Under-1 MW PV was not tested at plant level; LBNL's distributed file was described, not downloaded.

attributes.note: EIA plant/generator points; USPVDB v4.0 polygons and points (ground-mounted, 1 MW+); LBNL points above 5 MW AC. Precision not given in numbers.
attributes.gap_note: Under 1 MW: no per-plant location in EIA files; LBNL's public file gives ZIP code only (guide read, file not downloaded). 213 of 6,553 USPVDB v4.0 records matched to EIA lie more than 5 km from the EIA point.

attributes.note: AC nameplate per generator (EIA-860, 860M); DC at STC (EIA solar sheet, USPVDB, LBNL). Basis kept per field. EIA estimates small-scale AC by state.
attributes.gap_note: Under 1 MW, capacity appears only as state estimates (EIA, 63,193 MW AC in August 2026) or as DC per system in LBNL's file (not downloaded). EIA plant scope is 1 MW combined nameplate or more.

attributes.note: 'Utility Name' (EIA-860) is the company running each plant day to day: 2,629 names at 7,309 plants. EIA-860M 'Entity Name' matches it for 97.7% of generators.
attributes.gap_note: No operator for under-1 MW PV. USPVDB and LBNL's utility-scale file have no operator field. The EIA Ownership sheet (owners, separate from operator) lists 1,386 PV plants, 98 with several owners; not used as operator.

attributes.note: Month and year of initial commercial operation per generator (EIA). USPVDB p_year copies EIA; LBNL 'Solar COD' is a full date per project above 5 MW AC.
attributes.gap_note: No per-plant date for under-1 MW PV in EIA; Tracking the Sun has an installation date, sometimes a proxy such as an incentive claim (guide read). Topaz: EIA first generator 04-2013, USPVDB 2014, LBNL COD 2014-10-31.

how_to_use.example_request: Download https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860/xls/eia8602025.zip and extract it into an empty folder. Open 3_1_Generator_Y2025.xlsx, sheet 'Operable' (header on the third line), and keep Technology = 'Solar Photovoltaic' and Status = 'OP'. Join 2___Plant_Y2025.xlsx, sheet 'Plant', on Plant Code for coordinates.
how_to_use.example_result: Topaz Solar Farm (Plant Code 57695), San Luis Obispo County, CA: 5 OP PV generators, 585.9 MW AC (752.1 MW DC), operator 'Topaz Solar Farms LLC', first generator in commercial operation 04-2013, point 35.405556, -120.068611.
steps: 1. Download the ZIP (23,622,347 bytes; SHA-256 2b27929d26cc1da9ad6a530da1cac6718cd8496098ee560c4d47cfffd96d08ba) and extract it into an empty folder.
2. Convert the XLSX sheets to CSV (GDAL ogr2ogr worked). Each sheet has a title line before the header.
3. Keep generators with Technology 'Solar Photovoltaic' and Status 'OP': 7,979 rows at 7,309 plants in this test.
4. Join by Plant Code to the Plant sheet for coordinates, county, state and Utility Name; join by Plant Code and Generator ID to the solar sheet for DC.
5. Take the commercial operation date from Operating Month and Operating Year (MM-YYYY) per generator; the plant date is the earliest of its generators.
reading_traps: Capacity in the generator sheet is AC nameplate. DC appears only in the solar sheet: 198,470.9 MW DC against 152,847.6 MW AC for the same operating set.
76 plants have PV under 1 MW AC. 47 also list other generators (for example gas turbines); 29 show none in this sheet, so their inclusion is not explained by this file.
'OA' (out of service, expected to return) and 'OS' (out of service, not expected to return) are not counted as operating: 15 and 5 PV generators in this file.
Coordinates are a central point of the property, not a boundary. Compare with USPVDB before using them as precise locations.
The Proposed sheet (planned generators) belongs to the permitting topic and was not used.

Plant sheet has 17,349 plants of all technologies; filter generators first. The Ownership sheet (4___Owner_Y2025.xlsx, sheet 'Ownership') covers 1,386 PV plants and lists owners, which can differ from 'Utility Name'.

problems: records_total counts generator rows of the 'Operable' sheet (all technologies); records_for_country counts solar PV generators with status OP.
Sheets begin with a title line; GDAL names the columns Field1 to Field73 at first, and the real header is the third line.
The file reflects status at 31 December 2025. The monthly file (September 2026) gives a later count.

Revision of 2026-11-19: ZIP downloaded again (SHA-256 identical); 7,979 generators, 7,309 plants, 152,847.6 MW AC, 198,470.9 MW DC (one generator without DC), 2,629 Utility Names, 76 plants under 1 MW AC of PV, 15 OA and 5 OS reproduced with a stdlib XLSX reader.

steps: 1. Download the XLSX (14,013,970 bytes) into an empty folder.
2. Convert the 'Operating' sheet with GDAL or an XLSX reader; skip the title and blank lines.
3. Keep PV generators with Status beginning '(OP)': 8,335 generators at 7,651 plants in this test.
4. Use the generator-level Latitude and Longitude directly; no join is needed for location.
5. Read sheet 'Operating_PR' for Puerto Rico: 230 operating generators of all technologies, 19 PV, 18 plants, 164.7 MW.
reading_traps: The file counts generators, not plants: 8,335 operating PV generators against 7,651 plant IDs.
The monthly file is later than the annual one: 339 operating PV generators carry an operating year of 2026.
'(OA)' (15) and '(OS)' (5) PV generators are not operating.
Puerto Rico is not in sheet 'Operating': national totals from that sheet exclude it.
Scope is 1 MW combined nameplate: 78 plants in this file have under 1 MW of PV, as other generators lift the plant above the threshold.

problems: The HTTP content type was not recorded for this download.
The 'Operating' sheet has a title line and a blank line before the header; the real header starts 'Entity ID'.

how_to_use.example_request: Download usgsuspvdb-2.0.zip from Zenodo (MD5 370720806e01053be0cddfbdceffd546), extract it into an empty folder and read uspvdb_v2_0_20240807.csv. Keep eia_id to join with EIA-860 Plant Code.
how_to_use.example_result: case_id 400246, Topaz Solar Farm (eia_id 57695), San Luis Obispo County, CA: p_cap_ac 585.9, p_cap_dc 752.1, p_year 2014, p_area 12,480,866 m2, p_img_date 2021-07-17, p_dig_conf 4, point 35.368633, -120.03261 (5.2 km from the EIA plant point).
steps: 1. Download the Zenodo archive (4,419,222 bytes) and check its MD5 against the record.
2. Extract it into an empty folder and treat the files as data.
3. Read uspvdb_v2_0_20240807.csv (4,185 rows). The dictionary file is an XLSX with a .csv name; convert it before reading.
4. Join on eia_id to the EIA Plant Code for operator and capacity checks (4,157 of 4,185 records matched in this test).
reading_traps: p_year equals the earliest EIA operating year in 3,889 of 4,157 matched plants, but Topaz shows 2014 against EIA 04-2013.
The representative point and the EIA central point differ: median 0.23 km, 118 plants above 5 km, and 224.9 km for eia_id 61089.
The dictionary (July 2024) names some columns differently from the CSV headers (p_fac for p_name, p_reg for p_pwr_reg, p_batt for p_battery).
22 records have AC capacity under 1 MW; all have DC capacity of at least 1 MW, so the threshold is on DC.

problems: USGS and ScienceBase pages returned HTTP 403 to this client (DOI resolution included). The test used the Zenodo archive, a third-party copy of v2.0 (Catalyst Cooperative).
The HTTP content type was not recorded for this download.
The archive contains the data version of August 2024; the current USGS version was not tested.
Revision of 2026-11-19: USGS now answers (HTTP 200) and v4.0 was downloaded from USGS; this archive was not downloaded again.

how_to_use.example_request: POST or GET https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter with a bounding box query: way["power"="generator"]["generator:source"="solar"](35.33,-120.12,35.46,-120.00); out tags center. Send a generic client identifier: the first request without one returned HTTP 406.

steps: 1. Run the bounding-box query above with a generic client identifier.
2. Read the element centres and tags; treat polygons as mapped geometry only.
3. Check operator, capacity and date against EIA-860 or USPVDB before using.
reading_traps: Crowd-sourced geometry: completeness and date of mapping are not documented here.
Absence of a tag (operator, capacity, start date) in the sample is not evidence that the value does not exist elsewhere.
